ensuring consistent lending decisions aligned with FirstUK Bank's risk appetite

name: Residential Mortgage

name: Mortgage Credit Risk
description: The risk associated with mortgage lending at FirstUK Bank, governed by specific appetite targets regarding loss ratios, default rates, and borrower constraints.
context: FirstUK Bank Mortgage Credit Risk Target

name: Maximum Loss Ratio — Target 0.5% annually (max £2.5k loss per £500k portfolio)
description: The annual maximum allowable loss ratio for the mortgage portfolio, capped at 0.5% or £2.5k per £500k of the portfolio.
context: Maximum Loss Ratio: 0.5% annually (max £2.5k loss per £500k portfolio)

name: Default Rate Target — <2%
description: The target threshold for active mortgages in default, which must remain below 2% at any given time.
context: Default Rate Target: <2% (max 2% of active mortgages in default at any time)

name: LTV Limit — Max 95%
description: The maximum Loan-to-Value (LTV) limit permitted to prevent negative equity scenarios.
context: LTV Limit: Max 95% (no negative equity scenarios)

name: Debt-to-Income Limit — Max 45%
description: The maximum allowable debt-to-income ratio acting as a constraint on borrower income.

name: Mortgage Product
description: The banking product subject to the credit risk framework and appetite targets described in the document.
context: FirstUK Bank Mortgage Credit Risk Target

name: Loss Ratio — Target <0.5%, Actual 0.23%
description: A quantitative risk indicator measuring the loss ratio for Q4 2025. The actual value of 0.23% is within the defined risk appetite threshold of less than 0.5%.

name: Default Rate — Target <2%, Actual 1.2%
description: A quantitative risk indicator measuring the default rate for Q4 2025. The actual value of 1.2% is within the defined risk appetite threshold of less than 2%.

name: Average LTV — Target <80%, Actual 72%
description: A quantitative risk indicator measuring the Average Loan-to-Value (LTV) for Q4 2025. The actual value of 72% is considered conservative against the target of less than 80%.

name: Debt-to-Income — Target <45%, Actual 38%
description: A quantitative risk indicator measuring the Debt-to-Income ratio for Q4 2025. The actual value of 38% is considered conservative against the target of less than 45%.

name: Mortgage Product
description: The banking product subject to the underwriting process, involving borrower assessment and property valuation.

name: Mortgage Borrower
description: The customer applying for a mortgage, whose identity, employment, income, and credit history are assessed during the application process.

name: Credit Risk
description: The risk associated with borrower creditworthiness, managed through an automated credit scoring system (0–100) that evaluates payment history, utilization, credit age, inquiries, and defaults.

name: Credit Score Range — 90–100 (Excellent/Very Low Risk)
description: A credit score threshold between 90 and 100 indicating very low risk, which triggers an Auto-Approve action if other criteria are met.
context: 90–100 | Excellent | Very Low | Auto-Approve (if other criteria met)

name: Credit Score Range — 80–89 (Good/Low Risk)
description: A credit score threshold between 80 and 89 indicating low risk, requiring Standard Underwriting.

name: Credit Score Range — 70–79 (Fair/Medium Risk)
description: A credit score threshold between 70 and 79 indicating medium risk, requiring Enhanced Review.

name: Credit Score Range — 60–69 (Poor/High Risk)
description: A credit score threshold between 60 and 69 indicating high risk, requiring Manager Review and potential decline.

name: Credit Score Range — <60 (Very Poor/Very High Risk)
description: A credit score threshold below 60 indicating very high risk, resulting in an automatic decline.

name: Credit Scoring Product/Process
description: The automated credit scoring mechanism used to assess borrower risk based on weighted factors including payment history and credit utilization.

name: Permanent Employment Qualification Factor — 2+ years: 100% of stated salary
description: The qualifying income factor for employees in permanent roles with two or more years of history is set at 100% of their stated salary.

name: Permanent Employment Qualification Factor — <2 years: 75% of stated salary
description: The qualifying income factor for employees in permanent roles with less than two years of history is reduced to 75% of their stated salary.

name: Contract Employment Qualification Factor — >1 year remaining: 75% of stated salary
description: Contract employees with more than one year remaining on their contract are qualified at 75% of their stated salary.
context: Contract, >1 year remaining | 75% of stated salary

name: Self-Employed Qualification Factor — 2+ years: 75% of average last 2 years
description: Self-employed individuals with at least two years of history are qualified based on 75% of their average income over the last two years.
context: Self-employed, 2+ years | 75% of average last 2 years

name: Self-Employed Qualification Factor — <2 years: Not acceptable
description: Self-employment with less than two years of history is deemed not acceptable for income qualification purposes.

name: Bonus and Commission Qualification Factor: 50% of average last 2 years
description: Income derived from bonuses or commissions is qualified at 50% of the average amount received over the last two years.

name: Rental Income Qualification Factor: 75%
description: Rental income is qualified at 75% to account for potential vacancy risks.

name: Dividend Income Qualification Factor: 100% (>2 years history)
description: Dividend income is qualified at 100% provided it is sustainable and has a history of more than two years.

name: Pension and Benefits Qualification Factor: 100%
description: Pensions and benefits are qualified at 100% if they are guaranteed and stable.

name: Credit Risk — Income Stability and Qualification
description: The risk associated with the stability and verification of a customer's income used to determine qualifying income for lending.
context: Assess income stability (stable job vs. new employment)

name: Mortgage Product
description: A mortgage product with a principal amount of £300,000, an interest rate of 4.5%, and a loan term of 25 years.

name: Debt-to-Income Ratio — Actual 41.5%
description: The calculated debt-to-income ratio for the assessment, derived from monthly debt obligations and gross income.
context: Debt-to-Income Ratio = (Monthly Debt + Mortgage) / Monthly Income

name: Credit Risk — Debt Assessment
description: The assessment of a customer's ability to service debt, specifically evaluating monthly obligations against gross income to determine creditworthiness.

name: Mortgage Loan-to-Value (LTV) Risk
description: The risk associated with the ratio of the mortgage amount to the property value. Risk levels are categorized from Low to Very High based on the LTV percentage, with ratios above 95% considered Very High Risk and likely to be declined.

name: Max LTV for Excellent Credit Grade — Limit 95%
description: The maximum allowable Loan-to-Value ratio for customers with an Excellent credit grade (90+), set at 95% with standard pricing.

name: Max LTV for Good Credit Grade — Limit 90%
description: The maximum allowable Loan-to-Value ratio for customers with a Good credit grade (80–89), set at 90% with a +0.25% rate premium.

name: Max LTV for Fair Credit Grade — Limit 85%
description: The maximum allowable Loan-to-Value ratio for customers with a Fair credit grade (70–79), set at 85% with a +0.50% rate premium.

name: Max LTV for Poor Credit Grade — Limit 80%
description: The maximum allowable Loan-to-Value ratio for customers with a Poor credit grade (60–69), set at 80%, though applications may be declined.

name: Mortgage Product
description: The banking product subject to LTV assessment and credit grade limits at FirstUK Bank.
context: FirstUK Bank LTV Limits by Credit Grade

name: Property Location Risk
description: Risk associated with the geographic location of the property, categorized by stability of values ranging from prime areas (low risk) to declining areas (high risk).
context: Location | Prime area, stable values | Growing suburban | Declining area

name: Property Type Risk
description: Risk based on the nature of the property, where houses and flats are considered low risk, while listed buildings or unusual properties are high risk.
context: Property Type | House, flat | Newer construction | Listed building, unusual

name: Property Condition Risk
description: Risk related to the physical state of the property, ranging from modern/good repair (low risk) to poor condition requiring repairs (high risk).
context: Condition | Modern, good repair | Average condition | Poor, repairs needed

name: Market Liquidity Risk
description: Risk concerning the ease of selling the property, with high risk assigned to properties that are hard to sell with few buyers.
context: Market Liquidity | Easy to sell, buyers | Moderate sales | Hard to sell, few buyers

name: Loan-to-Value (LTV) Ratio
description: A quantitative metric used to confirm that the property valuation supports the loan amount; a valuation lower than the purchase price triggers a higher LTV.

name: Mortgage Product
description: The banking product subject to property valuation and risk assessment processes, involving LTV ratios and purchase price validations.

name: Composite Risk Score — Actual 81.1
description: The final calculated composite risk score derived from weighted components including credit score, income stability, debt-to-income, and LTV ratio. The current calculated value is 81.1.

name: Credit Score — Actual 82
description: A component of the composite risk score with a 40% weighting, currently scoring 82.

name: Income Stability — Actual 85
description: A component of the composite risk score with a 25% weighting, currently scoring 85.

name: Debt-to-Income — Actual 75
description: A component of the composite risk score with a 20% weighting, currently scoring 75.

name: LTV Ratio — Actual 80
description: A component of the composite risk score with a 15% weighting, currently scoring 80.

name: Credit Risk Rating Framework
description: A risk interpretation framework that categorizes composite scores into ratings (Excellent, Good, Fair, Poor, Very Poor) to determine the required approval authority.

name: Credit Risk — Underwriting Decision Matrix
description: The bank's formal framework for managing credit risk through a decision matrix based on Credit Score, Income DTI, and LTV. It defines the thresholds for approval, conditional approval, and decline to mitigate default risk.
context: Use This Matrix to Make Lending Decisions

name: Credit Score Thresholds for Lending Decisions
description: Quantitative credit score thresholds used to determine loan eligibility, ranging from 'Strong candidate' (90+) to 'Very high risk' (<60).

name: Income Debt-to-Income (DTI) Thresholds
description: Income DTI percentage limits used in the underwriting matrix to assess borrower affordability, with thresholds ranging from <35% to 45%.

name: Loan-to-Value (LTV) Thresholds
description: LTV percentage thresholds used to determine the collateral adequacy for lending decisions, with limits ranging from <75% to <90%.

name: Underwriting Approval and Decline Logic
description: The formal governance logic for lending decisions, categorizing outcomes as APPROVE, CONDITIONAL, or DECLINE based on the intersection of credit score, DTI, and LTV.

name: Communicate conditions to borrower
description: A required task within the condition management process to ensure the borrower is informed of the requirements for conditional approval.

name: Set deadline for condition satisfaction
description: A task to establish a timeframe for the borrower to meet approval conditions, typically set to 10 days.
context: Set deadline for condition satisfaction (typically 10 days)

name: Track conditions in system
description: A requirement to maintain a systemic record of the conditions associated with a conditional approval.

name: Release funds only after all conditions met
description: A critical control action ensuring that funds are not disbursed until all specified conditional approval requirements are satisfied.
context: Release funds only after all conditions met

name: Document condition satisfaction
description: A task to formally record that the conditions for approval have been successfully met.

name: Mortgage Credit Risk — Conditional Approval Process
description: The risk associated with lending where approval is contingent upon the verification of financial documentation, property reports, and debt reduction.
context: Approved upon receipt of recent bank statements
Approved upon payoff of auto loan

name: Mortgage Product
description: The banking product subject to the conditional approval process, involving property reports and down payments.
context: Approved upon borrower increasing down payment

name: Credit Default Risk
description: Risk associated with borrowers having a very high probability of default, specifically triggered by a credit score below 60.

name: Minimum Credit Score Threshold — Mandatory Decline <60
description: The minimum acceptable credit score for mortgage applications; scores below 60 result in a mandatory decline without review.

name: Debt-to-Income (DTI) Ratio Threshold — Mandatory Decline >45%
description: The maximum allowable Debt-to-Income ratio; applications exceeding 45% are deemed unaffordable and mandatorily declined.

name: Loan-to-Value (LTV) Ratio Threshold — Mandatory Decline >95%
description: The maximum allowable Loan-to-Value ratio; applications exceeding 95% are declined due to lack of an equity cushion.

name: Fraud and Misrepresentation Risk
description: Risk of application fraud or misrepresentation of facts by the borrower, leading to mandatory application decline.

name: Criminal History Risk
description: Risk associated with the adverse criminal history of an applicant, resulting in a mandatory decline.

name: Bankruptcy Risk
description: Risk associated with recent bankruptcy filings within the last 2 years, leading to mandatory application decline.

name: Discretionary Credit Score Range — 60–69
description: A credit score range where decline is discretionary and may be waived with senior approval if exceptional other credentials are provided.

name: Employment Stability Risk
description: Risk associated with applicants having less than one year of employment in an unstable field, categorized as a discretionary decline factor.

name: Market Decline Risk
description: Risk associated with properties located in high-risk declining markets, categorized as a discretionary decline factor.

name: Self-Employment Data Risk
description: Risk associated with self-employed applicants with less than 2 years of history, resulting in marginal data for assessment.

name: Mortgage Product
description: The banking product subject to the decline scenarios and application review process described in the document.
context: We have reviewed your mortgage application

name: Lending Team
description: The department responsible for reviewing mortgage applications and issuing decline notifications.

name: Final Walkthrough by Borrower and Appraiser
description: A pre-disbursement requirement ensuring the borrower and appraiser conduct a final walkthrough to confirm no major changes have occurred to the property.
context: Final walkthrough by borrower and appraiser (no major changes)

name: Final Verification of Employment
description: A mandatory pre-disbursement check requiring a phone call to verify employment 1–2 days before the closing date.
context: Final verification of employment (phone call 1–2 days before closing)

name: Final Credit Check
description: A final review of the borrower's credit to ensure no new derogatory marks or additional debt have been incurred prior to fund release.
context: Final credit check (no new derogatory marks, new debt)

name: Title Search Confirmation
description: Verification that the title search confirms a clear title, specifically ensuring there are no liens or claims against the property.
context: Title search confirms clear title (no liens, claims)

name: Insurance Policy Procurement
description: Requirement to ensure that the necessary insurance policy has been both obtained and paid for before funds are released.

name: Satisfaction of All Conditions
description: A comprehensive check to ensure that all conditions precedent to the loan disbursement have been fully satisfied.

name: Closing Disclosure Review and Signature
description: The final step in the pre-disbursement process requiring the closing disclosure to be reviewed and signed.

name: Mortgage Product
description: The banking product associated with the disbursement and post-approval process, involving appraisers, title searches, and closing disclosures.
context: Final walkthrough by borrower and appraiser

name: Mortgage Product
description: The bank's mortgage product, specifically regarding the servicing and post-approval monitoring phase of the product lifecycle.

name: Mortgage Credit Risk
description: The risk associated with mortgage creditworthiness, managed through annual re-scoring and ongoing credit monitoring.

name: Property Valuation Frequency — Every 3 Years
description: A quantitative requirement for property value tracking, specifying that valuations must be conducted every 3 years.

name: Credit Re-score Frequency — Annually
description: A quantitative monitoring requirement for credit risk, specifying that re-scoring must occur on an annual basis.

name: Default Early Warning Action
description: A specific trigger-based action where a missed payment initiates a default early warning process.
context: Default early warning (missed payment triggers action)

name: Credit Risk — Borrower Default
description: The risk of financial loss occurring when a borrower fails to make scheduled payments, leading to a formal declaration of default and potential foreclosure proceedings.
context: If Sale Price < Loan Balance: FirstUK Bank absorbs loss

name: Loss Calculation Metric — Loan Balance minus Sale Proceeds
description: A quantitative measure used to determine the bank's absorbed loss when the net proceeds from a property sale are insufficient to cover the remaining loan balance.
context: If Sale Price < Loan Balance: FirstUK Bank absorbs loss

name: Mortgage Loan Product
description: A lending product secured by property, subject to a specific loss mitigation timeline and foreclosure process upon borrower default.
context: Loan Modification — Change terms (extend, reduce rate)

name: Fair Lending Compliance Risk
description: The risk associated with ensuring lending decisions are based on credit criteria and not on protected characteristics such as race, religion, or gender identity.
context: FirstUK Bank Does NOT Consider: Race, color, national origin Religion Sex, gender identity Age (except as required by law) Marital status Disability (must accommodate)

name: Fair Lending Documentation Maintenance
description: Requirement to maintain records that demonstrate lending decisions are based on credit criteria rather than protected characteristics.
context: Documentation: Keep records demonstrating decisions based on credit criteria, not protected characteristics.

name: Default Risk related to Debt-to-Income (DTI) Ratio
description: The risk of loan default associated with high Debt-to-Income (DTI) ratios, which persists regardless of the applicant's credit score.
context: High DTI increases default risk regardless of credit score

name: Loan-to-Value (LTV) Risk
description: The risk associated with approving loans at maximum Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratios without corresponding strength in the applicant's credit and income profile.
context: Approve at max LTV without strong credit and income
Higher LTV requires stronger credit and income profile

name: Failure to Weight Recent Payment History
description: An identified weakness where recent late payments are overlooked. The correct procedure requires weighting activity from the last 24 months more heavily.

name: Standard Approval Credit Score Threshold — Score 75+
description: The minimum credit score required for a loan application to qualify for Standard Approval processing.

name: Standard Approval Debt-to-Income (DTI) Threshold — DTI <40%
description: The maximum Debt-to-Income ratio permitted for a loan application to be processed under the Standard Approval workflow.

name: Standard Approval Loan-to-Value (LTV) Threshold — LTV <85%
description: The maximum Loan-to-Value ratio permitted for a loan application to be processed under the Standard Approval workflow.

name: Credit Risk — Lending Approval Scenarios
description: The management of credit risk through a tiered approval authority structure based on borrower profiles, including standard, conditional, and enhanced reviews.

name: Standard Approval Authority Decision
description: Formal authority granted to CSRs and Underwriters to approve loans meeting specific credit, DTI, and LTV criteria within a 2–3 day timeline.
context: Standard Approval (Score 75+, DTI <40%, LTV <85%) | CSR/Underwriter | 2–3 days

name: Conditional Approval Authority Decision
description: Formal authority granted to Managers to approve loans with minor conditions and good credit within a 3–5 day timeline.
context: Conditional Approval (Minor conditions, good credit) | Manager | 3–5 days

name: Enhanced Review and Decline Authority Decision
description: Formal authority granted to the Risk Manager to handle enhanced reviews for fair credit/edge cases and to issue declines for weak profiles.
context: Enhanced Review (Fair credit, edge cases) | Risk Manager | 5–7 days

name: Appeal Authority Decision
description: Formal authority granted to the Head of Lending to resolve borrower disputes regarding loan declines within a 10-day timeline.
context: Appeal (Borrower disputes decline) | Head of Lending | 10 days
